title: Admin Taproot: contextual shortcuts and tasklet pipeline for support automation
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Summary: Build 'Taproot' — a minimal, contextual admin shortcut surface that converts common support actions into auditable, idempotent tasklets backed by a tasklet-runner pipeline. The goal is to reduce time-to-remediate for first-line support while preserving safety via permission gating, dry-run, and automatic telemetry.

Scope:
- Frontend: small contextual menu in the Support Console that suggests 3–6 vetted shortcuts (e.g., 'flush prefix cache', 'restart model-worker', 'reindex user embeddings').
- Backend: tasklet definition schema + tasklet-runner API that accepts typed inputs and returns a structured execution record.
- Safety: RBAC gating, dry-run and explicit confirmation flows, audit logging to tenant audit stream.
- Observability: per-tasklet telemetry (latency, success rate, tokens affected) and a dashboard surface for regressions.

Out of scope: building a generic automation DSL, long-running orchestrations (multi-step sagas) — those will be separate follow-ups. This iteration focuses on short, atomic admin actions that can be made idempotent within 30s–2m execution windows.
proposal: Design a single minimal schema for tasklets: {id, name, description, inputs: typed, prechecks: optional, executor: runtime-target, rollback_hint}. Implement a standalone tasklet-runner service (internal API) that validates RBAC, runs a sandboxed dry-run (if requested), records an immutable execution event to the audit log, and emits metrics to telemetry. Wire the Support Console to present contextual suggestions via a lightweight intent-matching heuristic (recent incident symptoms + route tags). Provide a developer workflow for adding new tasklets (PR -> automated integration tests -> ops review -> canary enablement).
tradeoffs:
- Simplicity vs flexibility: keep initial schema small to accelerate adoption; complex multi-step flows deferred.
- Safety vs speed: require explicit confirmation and dry-run opt-in for high-risk tasklets; low-risk ones allowed single-click with audit.
- Scope creep: avoid building a full orchestration engine; rely on existing runbook automations for multi-step processes.
implementation_plan: 1) Tasklet schema RFC + open review (2 days). 2) Tasklet-runner prototype (Go): HTTP API, RBAC checks, dry-run harness, audit write (7 days). 3) Support Console integration: contextual UI and intent matcher (4 days). 4) Telemetry + dashboard: metrics, tracing, and per-tasklet SLOs (3 days). 5) Add 6 initial vetted tasklets and internal canary with SRE + support (4 days). 6) Post-canary adjustments and GA (2 days).
acceptance_criteria: Support Console surfaces contextual shortcuts for at least three distinct support scenarios
Tasklet-runner accepts typed inputs, enforces RBAC, returns deterministic status and emits an immutable audit event
Dry-run mode simulates effects and logs precheck output without mutating state
Telemetry dashboard shows per-tasklet success rate, average latency, and error traces
All production tasklets have automated tests and an ops review recorded (Confluence/PR)
risks_and_mitigations: Accidental destructive actions: mitigation=mandatory audit trail + role gating + dry-run for medium/high risk
Tasklet proliferation causing cognitive overload: mitigation=tasklet review board + naming conventions + usage gating
Permission escalation attacks: mitigation=attach token-scoped ephemeral credentials and require 2-person approval for 'dangerous' tasklets
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): enable Taproot for internal Support team only; include a feature-flag with per-user opt-in. Monitor metrics for 72h (success rate, median latency, number of dry-runs vs executes). Phase B: expand to Customer Support users in staging orgs. Phase C: GA with on-call SRE escalation rules and guided runbooks for edge-cases.
